discovery: The Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality class of kinetic roughening and its exact solution
subfield: Statistical physics of non-equilibrium and disordered systems
motivation: The 1986 Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation established that growing interfaces far from equilibrium, from burning paper and bacterial colonies to imbibition fronts and turbulent liquid crystals, belong to a single universality class with non-trivial scaling exponents. Kardar and Zhang also connected it to directed polymers in random media, a central paradigm for disorder. Spohn, with collaborators, later derived exact height distributions given by Tracy-Widom statistics and the full scale-invariant KPZ fixed-point structure, predictions confirmed quantitatively in liquid-crystal turbulence, colloidal deposition and, recently, in polariton condensates and quantum spin chains. This work turned noisy, messy growth into one of the most precisely understood non-equilibrium phenomena in physics, showing that universality extends beyond equilibrium criticality. Giorgio Parisi, already a laureate, shares the original discovery; I nominate his co-authors and the leading architect of its exact solution.
